# Shared RCA MCP servers and tool permissions

Moved verbatim from `CLAUDE.md` to keep that file lean. Read it only when working on this topic.

## Weekly maintenance

`/rca-maintenance` (skill) or `make rca-health` runs `scripts/rca-health.sh`. It costs no model tokens and saves a report to `data/rca-health/<date>.md` (gitignored, sizes and names only). It does three things:

- **Tool drift.** It replays the harness's `deferred_tools_delta` records in the newest session transcripts and lists tools that are in neither `allow`, `deny`, nor `.claude/skills/rca-maintenance/keep-on-prompt.txt`. New write-like tools should be denied. It also lists allowed tools that servers no longer offer. Deny is by exact name, so a tool a server adds later is not blocked until this check runs.
- **Laya.** Compares the pinned version in `compose/laya/compose.yml` with PyPI and reports the container state.
- **Token stats.** Per `/ticket-rca` run: real token usage from the transcript, result sizes per tool, repeated calls, and long runs.

`ticket-rca` runs `rca-health.sh due` at the end and reminds the user when the last full run is over seven days old. The script reads the Claude Code transcript format (`~/.claude/projects/<repo>/*.jsonl`), which can change between versions. If the stats come back empty after an update, check the row shapes first.

- **Shared RCA MCP servers (Grafana, etc.) and their tool permissions**: `.mcp.json` is gitignored and must stay that way — `make start` writes each stack's `x-api-key` header into it, so committing it would publish those keys. Shared, non-stack servers are instead registered per machine by `bash scripts/setup-mcps.sh` (idempotent; add new servers to its `SERVERS` array), then signed in with `/mcp` (OAuth tokens are stored per machine by Claude Code, never in the repo). Their allow/deny tool rules live in the **tracked** `.claude/settings.json` (the rest of `.claude/`, including `settings.local.json`, is gitignored — keep it that way, it holds stack API keys in its allow rules). Never put a secret in `.claude/settings.json`. Every RCA MCP server is **read-only by policy**: only named read tools are allowed, every write tool is denied by exact name (new write tools Pylon/Notion/Linear add later are not denied by name, so read any permission prompt before approving). GitHub is also read-only: `scripts/hooks/block-gh-writes.js` (a PreToolUse hook on Bash, needs `node`) allows only an allowlist of read-only `gh` commands and blocks `gh api` with fields/non-GET methods, `gh api graphql`, and `git push`; `.claude/settings.json` also denies the common `gh` write verbs as a backup in case the hook cannot run. The hook scans the whole command text, so it can also block a harmless command that merely contains something like `gh issue create` in a string. To allow another read-only `gh` command, add it to `READ_ONLY` in the script. The ticket-RCA workflow lives in tracked skills under `.claude/skills/` (`ticket-rca`, `write`, `instance-logs`; start with `/ticket-rca <pylon-number>`), not in this file, so it only loads when a ticket is in play.
